mainTopic: רבי עקיבא's three rules, the ברייתא on בל יראה and בל ימצא, and when a גוי's חמץ in a Jew's care is forbidden
overview: The amud opens by listing three rules that follow from רבי עקיבא's earlier proof: ביעור חמץ is only by burning, הבערה לחלק יצאת, and we do not apply מתוך to allow burning on יום טוב that is not for food. Next comes a ברייתא that asks why the Torah needs both בל יראה and בל ימצא. Using the words לך, בבתיכם and בכל גבולך, it rules that your own חמץ is forbidden, including hidden חמץ and deposits taken from a גוי, while the חמץ of others and of הקדש is not your concern. A גזירה שוה on the word 'שאור' then makes houses and borders follow the same rules. The גמרא goes back to one line of the ברייתא about a conquered גוי who lives with you. אביי reverses the line, and רבא reads it as a leniency based on the double ״לְךָ״. Then the גמרא resolves an apparent contradiction about a גוי's deposits: they are forbidden only when the Jew accepted אחריות, as רבא told the people of מחוזא. The גמרא asks how this works for the view that דבר הגורם לממון is not like ממון, and answers that ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״ makes חמץ an exception. A second version of that discussion begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Three rules learned from רבי עקיבא's proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pulls three practical rules out of רבי עקיבא's earlier argument. They are: ביעור חמץ is only by burning, הבערה was singled out to divide the מלאכות, and we do not say מתוך שהותרה לצורך הותרה נמי שלא לצורך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from רבי עקיבא. First, the only way to destroy חמץ is by burning it. Second, kindling fire was singled out in the Torah to show that each מלאכה is counted separately. Third, we do not say that since kindling is allowed on יום טוב for a real need (like cooking), it is also allowed when there is no such need.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up the previous discussion. It lists three rules that we can learn from how רבי עקיבא built his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא proved that חמץ is forbidden from the 14th. His reasoning was that the 'first day' cannot be the 15th, because on יום טוב you cannot burn the חמץ. That reasoning only works if three things are true: חמץ must be destroyed by burning, הבערה counts as a real מלאכה on its own, and burning that is not for food is not permitted just because cooking fire is.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude
Destroying/removing chametz
Burning
Kindling was singled out to divide the מלאכות (each counts separately)

keyTerms.term: הוֹאִיל וְהוּתְּרָה לְצוֹרֶךְ הוּתְּרָה נָמֵי שֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ
keyTerms.meaning: Since it was permitted for a need, it is also permitted without a need (the principle of מתוך)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's proof rests on three rules: ביעור חמץ is only by burning, הבערה is its own מלאכה, and we do not apply מתוך to allow burning on יום טוב that is not for food.
steps.confusionAlert: 'לחלק יצאת' does not mean kindling is a lesser מלאכה. It means the Torah singled it out to teach that every מלאכה brings its own separate liability. The other view says it was singled out to teach that kindling is only a לאו and not a capital offense.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three rules are each debated elsewhere in שס. Here we see that רבי עקיבא's position commits him to one side of each debate.

phrases.english: Learn from Rabbi Akiva three things.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: אֵין בִּיעוּר חָמֵץ אֶלָּא שְׂרֵיפָה,
phrases.english: Learn from it: the removal of chametz is only by burning,
phrases.notes: If crumbling it also worked, you could do that on יום טוב, and the proof wouldn't hold up.

phrases.english: and learn from it: kindling was singled out to divide (the labors),
and learn from it: we do not say,
'Since kindling was permitted for a need (food preparation) —
it was also permitted not for a need.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier סוגיא about רבי עקיבא's derivation that חמץ is forbidden from the 14th.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא's proof assumes: burning is the only ביעור, הבערה לחלק יצאת, and no מתוך for burning that is not for food.

steps.title: Why does the Torah need 'shall not be found'?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes 'לא ימצא בבתיכם' and asks why it is needed, since the Torah already wrote 'לא יראה לך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'For seven days, leaven shall not be found in your houses.' Why does the verse need to say this? Didn't it already say, 'No leaven shall be seen with you, and no חמץ shall be seen with you, in all your borders'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts with a ברייתא. It points out that two verses seem to say the same thing and asks why both are needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that the Torah does not repeat itself for no reason. So if both בל יראה and בל ימצא exist, each must teach something the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Shall not be found (the source of בל ימצא)
Shall not be seen (the source of בל יראה)
What does the verse come to teach? (asks why a verse is needed)
Sourdough/leavening agent

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"Seven days leaven
shall not be found in your houses."
Why does the verse need to state this?
Wasn't it already stated:
"No leaven shall be seen with you,
and no chametz shall be seen with you, in all your borders"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ברייתא, unrelated to רבי עקיבא's three rules.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does לא ימצא add beyond לא יראה?

steps.title: 'Shall not be found' forbids hidden chametz and deposits from a gentile
steps.stepSummary: From 'לא יראה לך' alone we would learn that only your own חמץ is forbidden. Other people's and הקדש חמץ would be allowed, and we might think one may hide חמץ or accept a גוי's deposit. 'לא ימצא' teaches that this is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says 'no leaven shall be seen with you', it means you may not see your own, but you may see that of others (non-Jews) and of הקדש. So I might think one may hide חמץ and accept deposits of חמץ from a גוי. That is why the verse says 'shall not be found'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. It shows that 'לא יראה' has a weak spot, and 'לא ימצא' closes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לך' in 'לא יראה לך' limits the איסור to your own חמץ. That might suggest that hidden חמץ, or a גוי's חמץ kept in your house, is fine. 'לא ימצא' focuses on חמץ simply being found in your home, so even hidden חמץ and deposits a Jew accepts responsibility for are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Yours (your own chametz)
Of others (here, non-Jews)
Of the Most High (consecrated property, הקדש)
He may hide
Deposits (items held for safekeeping)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'יכול' (I might think) part is not the final הלכה. It is the mistaken idea the verse comes to reject. The conclusion is that hiding חמץ and accepting deposits from a גוי are forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the הלכה that a Jew may not keep a גוי's חמץ that he is responsible for, even though seeing a גוי's חמץ is permitted.

phrases.english: Because it is stated: "No leaven shall be seen with you" —
your own you may not see,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה רוֹאֶה שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים וְשֶׁל גָּבוֹהַּ.
phrases.english: but you may see that of others and that of the Most High (הקדש).

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יַטְמִין וִיקַבֵּל פִּקְדוֹנוֹת מִן הַגּוֹי —
phrases.english: I might think one may hide (chametz) and accept deposits from a gentile —
therefore the verse says "shall not be found."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why לא ימצא is needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לא יראה would allow others' חמץ, which might lead to allowing hidden חמץ or a גוי's deposits. לא ימצא forbids these.

steps.title: What about a gentile under your control living in your courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the derivation so far covers only a גוי who is independent and does not live with you. It asks for a source that includes a גוי you control who lives in your courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this about a גוי whom you have not conquered and who does not live with you in the courtyard. How do we know the same about a גוי whom you have conquered and who lives with you in the courtyard?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes its derivation one step further. It asks whether the איסור also covers חמץ of a גוי who is under your authority and shares your courtyard. This sets up the next verse-word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think 'לא ימצא' covers only the plain case. As written, the ברייתא treats the גוי who is dominated by you and lives on your property as the case that needs a further source. Note that in step 12 the גמרא will object that this order looks backwards, since this גוי's חמץ is closer to you and should be the more obvious case.

keyTerms.meaning: I have only (this case so far)
You conquered/subdued him
Dwells with you in the courtyard
From where do we know?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּגוֹי שֶׁלֹּא כִּיבַּשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: I have only a gentile whom you did not conquer,
and who does not dwell with you in the courtyard.
A gentile whom you conquered and who dwells with you in the courtyard —
from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּגוֹי שֶׁלֹּא כִּיבַּשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the derivation to a harder case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that includes a conquered גוי living in your courtyard?

steps.title: 'In your houses' includes even the gentile living with you
steps.stepSummary: The word 'בבתיכם' teaches that חמץ may not be found anywhere in your houses, even in the case of a conquered גוי living in your courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'shall not be found in your houses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the word 'בבתיכם' (in your houses). Any חמץ in your home area is included in the איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בבתיכם' widens the scope from 'חמץ that is yours' to 'חמץ located in your houses'. So even the case of the conquered גוי in your courtyard is covered.

keyTerms.meaning: In your houses
The verse teaches (introduces the proof-text)

steps.whatToRemember: בל יראה alone would cover only your own חמץ. לא ימצא adds hidden חמץ and a גוי's deposits. בבתיכם adds even a conquered גוי living in your courtyard.

phrases.english: The verse states: "It shall not be found in your houses."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the conquered גוי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word בבתיכם includes any חמץ found in your houses, even in that case.

steps.title: What about chametz outside the house?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'בבתיכם' only covers houses, and asks for a source for חמץ in pits, ditches and caves.
steps.simpleTranslation: From 'in your houses' I only know about חמץ that is in your houses. Where do we learn about חמץ in pits, ditches and caves?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא notices that the word 'בבתיכם' talks about houses. It asks what the law is for open places you own that are not houses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 used 'בבתיכם' to include every house, even one where a conquered גוי lives. But a pit or a cave is not a house at all. So the word 'בבתיכם' cannot cover it, and a new source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (from this verse) about...
Pits (round holes dug in the ground)
Ditches (long, narrow trenches)
Caves

phrases.english: I only know about what is in your houses.
From where do we know about pits, ditches and caves?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 5 stretched 'בבתיכם' to cover all houses. This step points out that the word still only means houses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that forbids חמץ in places you own that are not houses, like pits, ditches and caves.

steps.title: 'In all your borders' covers every place you own
steps.stepSummary: The words 'בכל גבולך' teach that the prohibition applies everywhere in your territory.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'in all your borders.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a different פסוק, 'ולא יראה לך שאר בכל גבולך', which talks about your whole territory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'גבולך' means everywhere that belongs to you, not only buildings. So חמץ in a pit or a cave is also forbidden. Now we have two pictures: חמץ 'in houses' and חמץ 'in borders.'

keyTerms.meaning: In all your borders, meaning your whole territory

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'in all your borders.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בכל גבולך' extends the prohibition to every place you own, including pits, ditches and caves.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two separate verses: one about houses and one about borders. The next question is built on the difference between them.

steps.title: The house rules and the border rules look different
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out that houses carry four prohibitions, while borders only forbid your own חמץ. It asks how we know to share the rules between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I can still say this. In houses, a person violates 'it shall not be seen,' 'it shall not be found,' 'do not hide it,' and 'do not accept deposits from a גוי.' In the borders, you may not see your own חמץ, but you may see חמץ of others and of הקדש. From where do we know to apply what was said about this place to that place, and what was said about that place to this place?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a problem. Each verse seems to carry its own details, so maybe each place has a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The house-verse (לא ימצא) taught the strict rules: no hiding and no accepting a גוי's deposit. The border-verse (לא יראה לך) taught a lenient detail: only your own חמץ is forbidden. So outside, maybe hiding is allowed, and inside, maybe even a גוי's or הקדש חמץ is forbidden. The ברייתא asks for a source to make both places follow the same rules.

keyTerms.meaning: And I can still say (a remaining problem)
Borders, meaning your territory outside the house
Belonging to 'the Most High', meaning הקדש (consecrated property)

keyTerms.term: לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
keyTerms.meaning: To apply what was said about one place to the other

steps.confusionAlert: 'You may see others' חמץ' only means you are not responsible for חמץ that is not yours. It does not allow hiding חמץ or accepting a גוי's deposit.

phrases.english: And I can still say:

phrases.aramaic: בַּבָּתִּים עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם בַּל יֵרָאֶה וּבַל יִמָּצֵא
phrases.english: In houses, one violates 'it shall not be seen' and 'it shall not be found,'

phrases.aramaic: וּבַל יַטְמִין וּבַל יְקַבֵּל פִּקְדוֹנוֹת מִן הַגּוֹי.
phrases.english: and 'do not hide it' and 'do not accept deposits from a גוי.'
phrases.notes: These strict rules came from 'לא ימצא' (Step 3).

phrases.english: In the borders, you may not see your own chametz,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה רוֹאֶה שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים וְשֶׁל גָּבוֹהַּ.
phrases.english: but you may see chametz of others and of הקדש.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִין לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
phrases.english: From where do we know to apply what was said about this place to that place,
and what was said about that place to this place?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that there are two separate verses (houses and borders), this step asks whether their details stay separate.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that applies the house rules (hiding, deposits) to the borders, and the border leniency (others' and הקדש חמץ) to the houses.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה brings the strict house rules to the borders
steps.stepSummary: The shared word 'שאור' in both verses creates a גזירה שוה. Because of it, all four house prohibitions also apply in the borders.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'leaven' and 'leaven' for a גזירה שוה. It says leaven about houses: 'leaven shall not be found in your houses.' And it says leaven about borders: 'leaven shall not be seen with you.' Just as with leaven said about houses, one violates 'not be seen,' 'not be found,' 'do not hide,' and 'do not accept deposits from גוים,' so too with leaven said about borders, one violates 'not be seen,' 'not be found,' 'do not hide,' and 'do not accept deposits from גוים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a גזירה שוה, which links two verses because they share the same word. First it copies the strict house rules to the borders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses use the word 'שאור.' A גזירה שוה teaches that the two verses explain each other. So hiding חמץ or taking a גוי's deposit is forbidden even outside the house.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah method that links two verses that use the same word, so a law in one also applies in the other
Sourdough, leaven (a strong leavening agent); the shared word here
Just as ... so too (the formula for comparing)

phrases.english: The verse teaches 'leaven' and 'leaven' for a verbal analogy.
Leaven is said about houses:
'Leaven shall not be found in your houses,'
and leaven is said about borders:
'Leaven shall not be seen with you.'
Just as the leaven said about houses:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם בַּל יֵרָאֶה וּבַל יִמָּצֵא
phrases.english: one violates 'not be seen' and 'not be found,'

phrases.aramaic: וּבַל יַטְמִין וּבַל יְקַבֵּל פִּקְדוֹנוֹת מִן הַגּוֹיִם,
phrases.english: and 'do not hide' and 'do not accept deposits from גוים,'
so too the leaven said about borders:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם בַּל יֵרָאֶה וּבַל יִמָּצֵא
phrases.english: one violates 'not be seen' and 'not be found,'

phrases.aramaic: וּבַל יַטְמִין וּבַל יְקַבֵּל פִּקְדוֹנוֹת מִן הַגּוֹיִם.
phrases.english: and 'do not hide' and 'do not accept deposits from גוים.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר שְׂאוֹר שְׂאוֹר לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of Step 8's question: house rules applied to borders.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shared word 'שאור' links the two verses, so all four prohibitions also apply in the borders.

steps.title: The same גזירה שוה brings the border leniency into the house
steps.stepSummary: Going the other way, the leniency that only your own chametz is forbidden also applies inside the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as with leaven said about borders, you may not see your own, but you may see חמץ of others and of הקדש, so too with leaven said about houses, you may not see your own, but you may see חמץ of others and of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the גזירה שוה in the opposite direction, answering the second half of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The border-verse taught that a גוי's or הקדש חמץ is not your problem. The גזירה שוה copies this leniency into the house too. Now both places have the same full set of rules: the four prohibitions, plus the exemption for חמץ that is not yours.

keyTerms.meaning: You may not see
Belonging to others (here, גוים)

steps.whatToRemember: Because of the גזירה שוה on 'שאור', houses and borders follow one set of rules. Your own חמץ is forbidden everywhere, and hiding חמץ or accepting a גוי's deposit is forbidden everywhere. חמץ of a גוי or of הקדש that you are not responsible for is allowed everywhere.

phrases.english: And just as the leaven said about borders:
you may not see your own,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה רוֹאֶה שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים וְשֶׁל גָּבוֹהַּ,
phrases.english: but you may see chametz of others and of הקדש,
so too the leaven said about houses:
you may not see your own,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה רוֹאֶה שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים וְשֶׁל גָּבוֹהַּ.
phrases.english: but you may see chametz of others and of הקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the גזירה שוה from Step 9 in the reverse direction, completing the answer to Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The leniency for others' and הקדש חמץ applies inside houses too.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Houses and borders share all the rules: four prohibitions on your חמץ, and an exemption for חמץ that is not yours.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical rule that a Jew does not have to remove a גוי's חמץ in his property, as long as he has not accepted responsibility for it.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא about a conquered gentile
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא. The line says that a gentile 'you conquered who lives with you' must be included through the verse ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: I would only know this about a gentile whom you did not conquer and who does not live with you in the courtyard. How do I know it about a gentile whom you did conquer and who lives with you in the courtyard? The verse says, "It shall not be found."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes this line from the ברייתא so that it can examine it. This is a setup for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the plain flow of the ברייתא, this line seems to continue the prohibition. It sounds like the חמץ of a far-away, unconnected gentile is obviously forbidden, and a verse is needed to include a gentile who is under your control. That order looks strange, and the next step attacks it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' The formula the גמרא uses to quote an earlier source in order to examine it.
You conquered him, meaning he is under your control.
He lives with you in the courtyard.
'It shall not be found.' The verse about chametz in your houses.

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּגוֹי שֶׁלֹּא כִּיבַּשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: I have only a gentile whom you did not conquer,
and who does not live with you in the courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי שֶׁכִּיבַּשְׁתּוֹ, וְשָׁרוּי עִמְּךָ בֶּחָצֵר מִנַּיִן?
phrases.english: A gentile whom you conquered and who lives with you in the courtyard, from where do we know?
The verse says: "It shall not be found."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא has ended. The גמרא now goes back to an earlier line of it (steps 4-5) to analyze it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A verse is needed to extend the rule from an unconnected gentile to a gentile who is conquered and lives with you.

steps.title: The order seems backwards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: 'The opposite!' If anything is forbidden, the חמץ of a gentile under your control is the more obvious case.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! (It is the other way around.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of the ברייתא. The case it treats as obvious seems less obvious than the case it needs a verse for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gentile who is under your control and lives with you is closely tied to you. So his חמץ should be the easier case to forbid. The ברייתא should start with him and use the verse to include the far-away gentile, not the other way around.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Toward the other side!' An expression meaning 'it is the reverse,' used when an argument seems backwards.

phrases.english: On the contrary! (It is the other way around!)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the order of the line quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the ברייתא's 'אין לי אלא... מנין' line.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The obvious case and the case needing a verse seem reversed. A gentile under your control is more tied to you, so his חמץ should be the easier case to forbid.

steps.title: אביי: Reverse the order
steps.stepSummary: אביי says to flip the two cases in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the objection by switching the order of the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the switch, the ברייתא reads: 'I would only know about a gentile you conquered who lives with you. How do I know about a gentile you did not conquer? The verse says לֹא יִמָּצֵא.' Now the obvious case comes first, and the verse extends the prohibition to the less obvious case.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it, flip the order.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Reverse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: switching the order of the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא, as written, treats the unconnected gentile as the obvious case of the prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Flip it. The conquered gentile who lives with you is the obvious case, and the verse extends the prohibition to the unconnected gentile.

steps.title: רבא: Keep the order. The line is about a leniency
steps.stepSummary: רבא does not reverse the text. He says the line goes back to the earlier clause, which allows seeing חמץ that belongs to others. It extends that leniency even to a gentile who is under your control.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, do not reverse it. The line refers back to the first clause: 'Your own חמץ you may not see, but you may see חמץ of others and חמץ of the Temple.' I would only know this about a gentile you did not conquer and who does not live with you in the courtyard. How do I know it about a gentile you conquered and who lives with you in the courtyard? The verse says, "It shall not be found."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He keeps the text as it is but connects it to the earlier leniency, not to the prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the line is about what is permitted, the order makes perfect sense. It is obvious that you may see the חמץ of a gentile who has no connection to you. The chief question is whether this is still true for a gentile under your control living with you. The verse teaches that even his חמץ is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, do not reverse it.
It refers back to the first clause.
Belonging to others, and belonging to the Temple (הקדש).

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the 'מנין' line as adding a prohibition. In רבא's reading it adds a leniency: the verse permits you to see a conquered gentile's חמץ.

phrases.english: Rava said: Really, do not reverse it,
and it refers back to the first clause:
Your own you may not see,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה רוֹאֶה שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים וְשֶׁל גָּבוֹהַּ.
phrases.english: but you may see that of others and that of the Temple.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּגוֹי שֶׁלֹּא כִּיבַּשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: I have only a gentile whom you did not conquer,
and who does not live with you in the courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי שֶׁכִּיבַּשְׁתּוֹ, וְשָׁרוּי עִמְּךָ בֶּחָצֵר, מִנַּיִן?
phrases.english: A gentile whom you conquered and who lives with you in the courtyard, from where do we know?
The verse says: "It shall not be found."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 12 than אביי gave in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the context: the line belongs to the earlier leniency, not to the prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line seems to continue the prohibition, which makes its order backwards.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line extends the leniency of seeing others' חמץ even to a gentile who is conquered and lives with you, so the order is correct.
steps.whyThisMatters: On this reading, the point is: you are not required to destroy חמץ that truly belongs to a gentile, even one who lives with you.

steps.title: How can a prohibition verse teach a leniency?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading. The ברייתא is trying to prove something is permitted, yet it quotes ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״, a verse that forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this תנא is looking for a leniency, and he brings a verse that teaches a prohibition?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's explanation. The proof verse does not seem to fit a leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״ means 'it shall not be found.' It is a source for forbidding חמץ, not for allowing it. So how can it prove you may see a conquered gentile's חמץ?

keyTerms.meaning: He is looking for a leniency (something permitted).
He brings a verse that teaches a prohibition.

phrases.english: But this Tanna is looking for a leniency,
and he brings a verse for a prohibition?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״ teaches a leniency.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse that forbids cannot be the source for something being permitted.

steps.title: The double ״לְךָ״ attaches to ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״
steps.stepSummary: The word ״לְךָ״ ('to you') appears twice. The extra one is attached to ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״, which teaches that only חמץ that is yours is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says ״לְךָ״ ״לְךָ״ two times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The proof is not really from the forbidding words. It comes from an extra word ״לְךָ״ that is read together with ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לֹא יֵרָאֶה לְךָ״ ('it shall not be seen for you') is written twice, so one ״לְךָ״ is extra. It is attached to ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״, giving 'it shall not be found for you.' This limits the prohibition to חמץ that is yours, so a gentile's חמץ is permitted even if he is under your control.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To you / yours.' Limits the prohibition to chametz that belongs to you.
Two times.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the ברייתא teaches a leniency. Because of the extra ״לְךָ״, only חמץ that belongs to you is forbidden. חמץ that belongs to a gentile, even one under your control who lives with you, is not included.

phrases.english: Because it says "to you," "to you"
two times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and supports רבא's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the real source: an extra word is attached to the verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof comes from the forbidding words ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״, which cannot teach a leniency.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof comes from the extra ״לְךָ״ attached to ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״. Only your own חמץ is forbidden, so a conquered gentile's חמץ is permitted.

steps.title: The ברייתא forbids hiding חמץ or accepting חמץ deposits from gentiles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא. It says one may not hide חמץ or accept deposits of חמץ from gentiles, based on ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: I might have thought a person may hide חמץ, or accept deposits of חמץ from gentiles. Therefore the verse says: 'It shall not be found.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the ברייתא so it can examine it. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line says that חמץ deposited with you by a gentile is forbidden. The verse ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״ ('it shall not be found') is used to forbid it, even when you only hide the חמץ or hold it for someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', the formula for quoting a line from a ברייתא already cited
He hides or conceals (the chametz)
Deposits, items left with someone for safekeeping
'The verse teaches', introduces the verse that answers the 'I might have thought'

phrases.english: The Master said: I might have thought one may hide (chametz)
and accept deposits (of chametz) from the gentiles,
therefore the verse says: 'It shall not be found.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: יָכוֹל יַטְמִין וִיקַבֵּל פִּקְדוֹנוֹת מִן הַגּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of ״לְךָ״ is resolved, the גמרא goes back to analyze another line of the ברייתא, the one from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gentile's חמץ that was deposited with a Jew is forbidden under ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״.

steps.title: Contradiction with the earlier clause that allows other people's chametz
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the first clause of the same ברייתא allowed seeing חמץ that belongs to others. So why are a gentile's deposits forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say in the first clause: 'Your own you may not see, but you may see חמץ of others and of the Temple'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the line it just quoted. It shows that the line seems to contradict the beginning of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא said only your own חמץ is forbidden, and other people's חמץ is allowed. A gentile's deposit belongs to the gentile, not to you. So it should be allowed, yet the later line forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But you said', points to a contradiction with an earlier statement
The first clause of the text
Belonging to the Most High, meaning consecrated property

phrases.english: But you said in the first clause:
'Your own you may not see,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה רוֹאֶה שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים וְשֶׁל גָּבוֹהַּ!
phrases.english: 'but you may see that of others and that of the Temple!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a gentile's חמץ deposit is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: the רישא allows חמץ that belongs to others, and a gentile's deposit belongs to others.

steps.title: The difference is whether he accepted responsibility
steps.stepSummary: Both lines are correct. The forbidden case is when the Jew accepted responsibility (אחריות) for the חמץ. The permitted case is when he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is where he accepted responsibility for it. That case is where he did not accept responsibility for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. It says the two lines are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Jew agreed to pay for the חמץ if it is lost or stolen, it is treated as if it were his own, so it is forbidden. If he did not agree to pay, it stays fully the gentile's, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult', the opening of a resolution
He accepted upon himself
Responsibility, a commitment to pay for loss or damage

steps.whatToRemember: A gentile's חמץ becomes forbidden for a Jew to keep once the Jew takes on אחריות (responsibility to pay for it).

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this (forbidden case) is where he accepted responsibility for it,
that (permitted case) is where he did not accept responsibility for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא based on whether אחריות was accepted)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any gentile's חמץ is 'of others' and is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the Jew accepts אחריות, the חמץ is treated as his own and is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא's instruction to the people of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא told the people of מחוזא to remove the soldiers' חמץ from their homes, because they would have to pay for it if it were lost or stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבא said to the people of מחוזא: 'Remove the חמץ of the soldiers from your houses. Since if it were stolen or lost, it stands in your possession and you would have to pay for it, it is considered like yours, and it is forbidden.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of רבא that matches the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of מחוזא were obligated to pay for the soldiers' חמץ if anything happened to it. רבא ruled that this obligation makes the חמץ count as theirs, so they had to get it out of their houses. This is the same idea as אחריות in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove (the chametz)
Members of the army, soldiers
It stands in your possession or responsibility
It is considered like your own

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר לְהוּ רָבָא לִבְנֵי מָחוֹזָא:
phrases.english: Like that which Rava said to the people of Mechoza:
'Remove the chametz of the soldiers from your houses.'
'Since if it were stolen or if it were lost,'
'it stands in your possession and you would have to pay —'
'it is considered like yours, and it is forbidden.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר לְהוּ רָבָא לִבְנֵי מָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 19 with a practical ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that accepting אחריות makes a gentile's חמץ count as one's own.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's instruction to the residents of מחוזא about the soldiers' חמץ.

steps.title: What about the view that a cause of monetary loss is not like money?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for the view that דבר הגורם לממון counts as ממון. But what can be said according to the view that it does not count as ממון?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says: something that causes money is like money. But according to the one who says it is not like money, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from steps 19-20. It asks whether that explanation only works according to one side of a known argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חמץ is treated as the Jew's only because he would have to pay for it. That is a case of דבר הגורם לממון, something that leads to money. Someone who holds this is not considered ממון cannot use that reason, so why would the חמץ be forbidden according to him?

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works well', the opening of a challenge that fits only one opinion
Something that causes a monetary result, such as an obligation to pay
It is considered like money (property)
'What can be said?', asking for an answer that fits the other view

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not rejecting the אחריות answer. It is only asking how that answer would work for the opinion that דבר הגורם לממון is not ממון.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
something that causes money is considered like money.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לָאו כְּמָמוֹן דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: But according to the one who says it is not considered like money,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דָּבָר הַגּוֹרֵם לְמָמוֹן כְּמָמוֹן דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind steps 19-20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that accepting אחריות makes the חמץ count as the Jew's own.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The idea depends on treating an obligation to pay (דבר הגורם לממון) as ownership, and not every opinion accepts that.

steps.title: Chametz is different because the verse says 'it shall not be found'
steps.stepSummary: Even if דבר הגורם לממון is not normally treated like ממון, חמץ is an exception. The פסוק ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״ forbids חמץ that is in the Jew's possession and under his responsibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because the verse said: 'It shall not be found.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 21. חמץ has a special rule because of the words ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, the גמרא asked how חמץ can be forbidden for the view that something which only causes a money loss does not count as real money. The answer is that the general monetary rule does not decide this case. The פסוק ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״ widens the איסור to חמץ that is simply 'found' with the Jew, as long as he carries אחריות for it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different here; this case has its own special rule
'It shall not be found' (Shemos 12:19), the verse forbidding chametz to be found in a Jew's possession
Responsibility to pay if the item is lost or stolen

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, חמץ the Jew is responsible for is forbidden according to everyone. Even the view that דבר הגורם לממון is not like ממון agrees, because of the פסוק ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying this חמץ becomes the Jew's money. It stays the gentile's חמץ. The פסוק simply adds an exception that forbids it anyway, because the Jew carries responsibility for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical rule that a Jew may not keep חמץ on פסח that he has accepted responsibility for, even if it belongs to a gentile.

phrases.english: It is different here,
phrases.notes: The גמרא answers by saying this case is an exception.

phrases.english: because [the verse] said: 'It shall not be found.'
phrases.notes: The word 'found' covers any חמץ located with the Jew that he is responsible for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21 by pointing to a special verse.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special scriptural exception (גזירת הכתוב) that overrides the general monetary principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For the view that דבר הגורם לממון is not like ממון, חמץ the Jew is only responsible for should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: חמץ is an exception. ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״ forbids it once the Jew carries אחריות for it.

steps.title: Second version: the answer fits the view that a cause of monetary loss is not money
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the discussion begins. It says the explanation works well for the view that דבר הגורם לממון is not like ממון, which sets up a challenge against the opposite view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version: This works out well according to the one who said that something which causes monetary loss is not considered like money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second version of the discussion and says which view the earlier answer fits. This line sets up the next move, a challenge against the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the question is turned around. For the view that דבר הגורם לממון is not like ממון, the פסוק ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״ is needed to forbid חמץ the Jew is responsible for, so the verse has a clear job. The coming line will ask about the opposite view: if such חמץ already counts as his own money, why would the פסוק be needed?

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; it introduces a second version of the discussion
It works out well; it fits
According to the one who said
It is not considered like money

steps.confusionAlert: In the first version, the trouble was with the view that it is not like money. In this second version, that view is the one that works well. The trouble now moves to the opposite view.

phrases.english: Some say [another version]:
This works out well according to the one who said
phrases.notes: The first half of a הניחא...אלא formula. The challenge to the other view will follow.

phrases.english: an item that causes monetary [loss]
phrases.notes: Here this means חמץ the Jew must pay for if it is lost or stolen.

phrases.english: is not considered like money,
phrases.notes: For this view, the verse is needed to forbid such chametz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a second version that reverses which view the answer fits best.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that דבר הגורם לממון is like ממון (to be attacked in the next line)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. If the answer fits the 'not like money' view because the verse is needed, the other view will seem to make ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא״ unnecessary.
